question.text: Following the November 18, 2024 amendments to the AIF Regulations on pro-rata and pari-passu rights, which of the following CLASS of entities may subscribe to a junior/subordinate class of units accepting lesser returns or higher losses in Category II AIFs?

answer.text: Any high-net-worth individual with AI status
Any mutual fund investing above INR 100 crore
Only the fund's employees and directors

The Manager/Sponsor of the AIF; Multilateral/Bilateral DFIs; State Industrial Development Corporations; entities owned or controlled by Central/State Government or foreign Governments (including central banks and SWFs)

explanation.text: The Logic: Post the priority-distribution ban (SEBI's 'pro-rata' rule), the following entities may subscribe to a junior/subordinate class of units in Cat I/II AIFs: (i) Manager or Sponsor of the AIF; (ii) Multilateral or Bilateral Development Financial Institutions; (iii) State Industrial Development Corporations; (iv) entities established/owned/controlled by Central/State Government or foreign Governments, including Central Banks and Sovereign Wealth Funds. If the Manager/Sponsor subscribes to junior class, no evergreening of their loans via investee companies is permitted. The Trap: Options A/B/C propose classes that cannot subscribe to subordinated units. HNIs and MFs, regardless of size, aren't in this exempt list. The anti-evergreening rule specifically protects against Manager-Sponsor self-dealing. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the pro-rata amendment. Distinct from Performance Fee/Carried Interest carve-out (which is NOT subject to pro-rata rule, since it's GP economics). Schemes pre-Nov-18-2024 with priority model are frozen from fresh commitments. Manager's Pro-Tip: DFI/Government SWF junior tranches are useful for 'credit enhancement' in debt funds and infra funds — the DFI takes first-loss to catalyse senior LP participation. Draft the subordination waterfall carefully in the Contribution Agreement to avoid SEBI flagging it as disguised priority distribution.
